newsitem.title: USA: U.S. retailers' profits rose in Q3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. retailers' profits rose in Q3.

text.p: After-tax profits of U.S. retailers rose to 2.0 cents per dollar of sales in the third quarter of 1996 from 1.7 cents per sales dollar in the second quarter, the Commerce Department said Wednesday.
By comparison a year earlier in the third quarter of 1995, retailers earned profits after taxes of 1.6 cents per dollar of sales.

Retailers generated total after-tax profits in the third quarter of $4.84 billion, up from $3.95 billion in the second quarter and also up from $3.59 billion a year earlier in the third quarter of 1995.
The Commerce Department based its findings on quarterly financial reports supplied by 547 corporations.
Retailers had total sales in the third quarter of $236.84 billion, up from $234.81 billion in the second quarter and also up from $221.49 billion in the third quarter of 1995, the department said.
The after-tax figures are for retailers with assets of $50 million or more and are not seasonally adjusted.
